title: Azure Cloud Shell Deep Dive
description: Explore Cloud Shell features including Azure Drive, persistent storage, file editing, and scripting in the browser.

data.text: **Azure Cloud Shell** is a browser-accessible, authenticated shell that runs in the Azure Portal or at shell.azure.com. It comes with the Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, and common tools pre-installed, so you can start working immediately.

data.title: What Cloud Shell Offers
items: **Pre-authenticated** — You are already logged in with your Azure account
**Bash and PowerShell** — Switch between the two environments
**Persistent storage** — Files are saved to an Azure Files share linked to your account
**Code editor** — Use `code` to open a built-in file editor inside the shell
**No local install needed** — Everything runs in the browser

data.text: Azure PowerShell includes an **Azure Drive** (the `Azure:` drive) that provides a file-system-like view of your Azure resources. You can navigate subscriptions, resource groups, and resources as if they were folders. This is only available in PowerShell, not Bash.

data.title: Using Azure Drive in Cloud Shell
data.code:
# Change to the Azure drive
Set-Location Azure:

# Navigate to a subscription
cd subscriptions

# Navigate to a resource group
cd MySubscriptionName/resourcegroups/MyResourceGroup

# List resources in the resource group
Get-ChildItem

# Navigate back to the storage drive
Set-Location $home
cd clouddrive

data.text: Cloud Shell mounts a 5 GB Azure Files share at `$HOME/clouddrive` (Bash) or `$home\clouddrive` (PowerShell). You can store scripts, configuration files, and templates here. Files you save persist between Cloud Shell sessions.

data.title: Cloud Shell Scripting Example
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# Save this as deploy.sh in your clouddrive

RESOURCE_GROUP="learn-rg-$(date +%s)"
LOCATION="eastus"

# Create a resource group
az group create --name $RESOURCE_GROUP --location $LOCATION

# Deploy an ARM template
az deployment group create \
  --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \
  --template-file ./template.json

# List resources in the new group
az resource list --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --output table

data.text: Cloud Shell includes a built-in editor. Run `code filename` to open a file for editing. You can create new files, edit existing ones, and save them to your persistent storage. The editor supports syntax highlighting for JSON, YAML, Bash, PowerShell, and more.

terms.definition: A browser-based, authenticated shell with Azure CLI, PowerShell, and persistent storage.
A PowerShell-only file-system view of Azure resources within Cloud Shell.
The persistent Azure Files share mounted in Cloud Shell for storing scripts and files.

data.title: Session Timeout
data.text: Cloud Shell sessions time out after 20 minutes of inactivity. Your files are safe because they are stored in Azure Files, but you will need to restart the session if you return later.
